name: Meridian Munitions Wheelgun-38 'Roundhouse'
description:
The Meridian Munitions Wheelgun-38 is a six-shot double-action revolver chambered in .38 Special, built with a carbon steel frame and a four-inch barrel. It is the cheapest revolver available in GLMZ, manufactured using the same cost-minimization approach that defines all Meridian Munitions products. The finish is a flat black oxide that provides minimal corrosion resistance, and the grips are hard rubber with no contouring.

The Roundhouse exists because a significant portion of GLMZ's Shelf population distrusts semi-automatic pistols. Revolvers are mechanically simpler — no magazines to lose, no slides to rack, no safeties to forget. For residents with minimal firearms training, the revolver's simplicity is its primary feature: load it, point it, pull the trigger. The heavy double-action trigger pull serves as both a safety mechanism and a quality-control compromise.

The weapon's reliability is its saving grace. Where a Payday might jam, a Roundhouse will fire. The .38 Special round provides adequate stopping power against unarmored targets, and the six-round cylinder doesn't require counting rounds or managing reloads under stress. For Shelf residents who want 'a gun that works when I need it to work,' the Roundhouse delivers on that promise and nothing more.
specifications:
caliber: .38 Special
effective_range: 25 meters
rate_of_fire: Double-action revolver
magazine_capacity: 6 rounds (cylinder)
weight: 0.74 kg
tactical_use: A basic defensive revolver offering simplicity and reliability at the cost of capacity and reloading speed. The double-action trigger is heavy but consistent. Six rounds of .38 Special provide adequate stopping power for unarmored threats. No external safety to disengage under stress. The revolver's simplicity makes it nearly malfunction-proof in untrained hands.
cultural_context: The Roundhouse is the Shelf purist's firearm. Its owners tend to view semi-automatic pistols with suspicion — too many moving parts, too many things that can go wrong. There's a generational divide at play: older Shelf residents overwhelmingly prefer revolvers, while younger residents gravitate toward semi-automatics. The Roundhouse is the old guard's weapon of choice.
story_hooks: An elderly Shelf shopkeeper defends their store with a Roundhouse and becomes an unlikely folk hero — but the attention draws scrutiny to their past that they've spent decades hiding.
A batch of Roundhouses is discovered with barrels bored out to accept .357 Magnum — a dangerous modification that the weapons weren't built to withstand.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian wheelgun with a classic revolver silhouette—compact and blocky rather than elegant. The Roundhouse reads as pure function: no frills, no aesthetic pretense. Its proportions are straightforward and squat, designed for someone who needs 'a gun that works,' not a collector's piece.
physical_description.dimensions: Barrel length: 10.2 cm. Overall length: 21.6 cm. Cylinder diameter: 3.8 cm. Compact enough to pocket-carry but substantial enough to feel like a real firearm.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but manageable—0.74 kg feels solid in the palm without being unwieldy. The carbon steel frame gives it honest weight, the kind that makes you aware you're holding something serious.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon steel frame and cylinder. Simple, robust, no exotic alloys. The construction is straightforward: steel that will rust if neglected but won't fail catastrophically under stress.
physical_description.finish: Flat black oxide coating—matte, non-reflective, minimal corrosion resistance. Designed for function, not longevity. Scratches and wear show easily against the dark surface.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black primary with natural steel showing through worn edges. Hard rubber grips in charcoal gray—no sheen, no contrast.
physical_description.grip_texture: Hard, uncontoured rubber—slightly textured but not aggressive. No ergonomic shaping; it's purely utilitarian. Grips feel cold and basic in hand, with subtle grip diamonds molded in for bare minimum traction.
distinctive_features: Simple fixed iron sights—minimal machining, front post and rear notch
Heavy double-action trigger with visible trigger guard—no safety to disengage
Six-round cylinder with visible cylinder latch pin
Simple ejector rod running beneath barrel
Minimal barrel underlug—no rail or accessory mounting
Visible machine marks where cost-cutting shows
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: MERIDIAN MUNITIONS stamped in utilitarian block letters on the left barrel. Serial number on the frame below the cylinder window. No logo flourishes—purely functional stamps.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn and pragmatic. The flat black oxide shows handling marks, micro-scratches, and minor holster wear. Not abused, but clearly a working gun that sees regular handling. No collector's care—it's a tool.
